title: College Football Week 10 Live Updates: Scores, Schedule, and CFP Rankings on NCAA.com
body:
The college football landscape shifted dramatically on Saturday as the noon kickoff slate delivered two stunning upsets, threatening the perfect records of two of the last three unbeaten FBS programs and setting the stage for a chaotic race to the College Football Playoff. While the nation’s top‑ranked teams battled for dominance, a surprise victory by a mid‑major program and a heartbreaking loss for a perennial powerhouse underscored the volatility that has come to define this season’s middle stretch.

In the early afternoon, the University of Texas Longhorns, entering the game as the sole remaining undefeated team from the Power Five, stumbled against the under‑dog Houston Cougars in a 31‑24 thriller at NRG Stadium. Texas, which had ridden a 12‑game winning streak into the matchup, was unable to contain Houston’s explosive offense, led by sophomore quarterback Jake “Lightning” Martinez, who threw for 342 yards and three touchdowns. The Longhorns’ defense, which had been among the nation’s best against the run, gave up 210 rushing yards, including a 78‑yard breakaway run by Houston’s freshman running back Malik Harris in the fourth quarter. The loss not only drops Texas to 9‑1 but also knocks them out of the top four in the CFP rankings, opening a critical window for teams like Alabama and Ohio State to vault back into contention.

Just moments later, the conference championship aspirations of the University of Washington were dealt a similar blow. The Huskies, sitting at 10‑0 and perched at No. 3 in the poll, faced a determined Boise State squad in a game that quickly turned into a defensive slugfest. Washington’s star quarterback, senior quarterback Tyler Jensen, was intercepted twice, and the team’s once‑reliable offensive line faltered under the pressure of Boise State’s relentless blitzes. The Broncos capitalized, securing a 27‑20 upset that not only ended the Huskies’ unbeaten run but also forced the CFP committee to reevaluate the top‑four picture as the regular season heads into its final stretch.

Meanwhile, the noon slate also featured several high‑profile matchups that proceeded as expected, reinforcing the status quo for a handful of elite programs. Alabama, still perched at No. 2, dispatched Mississippi State 38‑14 in Tuscaloosa, with Heisman‑candidate quarterback Bryce Caldwell throwing for 410 yards and five touchdowns. Ohio State, holding steady at No. 4, rolled past Purdue 45‑17, showcasing a balanced attack that combined a 250‑yard rushing performance from junior running back Elijah Brooks with a 320‑yard aerial display from sophomore quarterback Mason Lee. Both victories kept the Buckeyes and Crimson Tide safely within the playoff conversation, but the margin for error has narrowed considerably after the upsets in Texas and Washington.

The ripple effects of these results were instantly reflected in the latest CFP rankings released Sunday morning. Texas fell to No. 7, Washington dropped to No. 9, while Boise State vaulted into the top‑12 for the first time this season. The new top‑four composition now reads: Alabama (1), Ohio State (2), Georgia (3), and Michigan (4). Georgia, which had previously been perched at No. 5, surged ahead after a dominant 42‑10 win over Kentucky, while Michigan reclaimed the No. 4 spot with a 31‑24 victory over Indiana that featured a last‑minute field goal by senior kicker Ryan Patel. The reshuffling underscores the increasingly tight race for the four coveted playoff berths, with several teams now needing to win out and hope for favorable outcomes in the remaining games.

Analysts point to the growing parity across the FBS as a key narrative heading into the final weeks. The success of programs like Houston and Boise State demonstrates that strong recruiting, innovative offensive schemes, and disciplined defense can level the playing field against traditional powerhouses. Moreover, the pressure on the remaining undefeated teams has intensified; a single misstep could see them relegated to the New Year’s Six bowls rather than the playoff. Coaches are now tasked with fine‑tuning game plans, managing player health, and navigating the psychological weight of heightened expectations.

Looking ahead, Week 11 promises a slate of must‑watch contests that could cement or dismantle the newly formed hierarchy. Alabama travels to face LSU in a potential de‑facto playoff preview, while Ohio State hosts Penn State in a rivalry that could determine the Big Ten’s representative. Meanwhile, Texas must rebound against a resilient Oklahoma State squad, and Washington seeks redemption against a top‑ten Oregon team in a Pac‑12 showdown. The outcomes of these games will likely finalize the playoff field, leaving fans and pundits alike on the edge of their seats as the season races toward its climax.
